title: Government Releases New UAP Documents
excerpt: The latest in a string of federal UAP document releases includes research tied to Skinwalker Ranch, as its owner describes a sighting.
content:
Live Poll

Do you trust the federal government to fully disclose what it knows about UFOs?

Government released new documents on Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAP) on a Friday, the latest in a string of such releases. Skinwalker Ranch owner Brandon Fugal called the release landmark and described his own sighting.

Why it matters

The release adds to a growing public record of government documents on unexplained aerial phenomena in the United States. Fugal's account of a sighting on his privately funded property places a first-hand claim alongside the official files.

The reported object was up to 50 feet long and saucer-shaped, and was seen about six months after Fugal purchased the ranch. The sighting is a first-hand account from the property owner, and the cause of the object has not been identified.

The players

Brandon Fugal

Fugal is the owner of Skinwalker Ranch in Utah, who has funded research on the property with tens of millions of his own dollars and does not accept government funding.

BAASS (Bigelow Aerospace Advanced Space Studies)

BAASS is a research company that, in a Ten-Month Report, selected Skinwalker Ranch as a site for frequent displays of advanced aerospace vehicles.

The details

Fugal reported seeing a gray silver, disc-like object hovering above the mesa in broad daylight, with multiple witnesses present. He described the object as moving extremely quickly and said it rendered a member of the ranch security team catatonic. Fugal funds the research on the property privately and reveals findings on the History Channel series The Secret of Skinwalker Ranch.

Timeline

  1. Six months after Fugal bought Skinwalker Ranch, he reported the hovering object sighting.

  2. On a Friday, November 20, 2026, the new government UAP documents were released.

Big Picture

The release continues a string of prior federal UAP document releases that have made government files on unexplained aerial phenomena publicly accessible. It extends that pattern while Skinwalker Ranch's privately funded research runs alongside the official record.

Public access to government UAP files lets readers review the official record directly rather than relying on summaries. Privately funded research at sites like Skinwalker Ranch is shared through television, so claims there reach audiences without peer review.

The takeaway

Official UAP document releases and privately funded field research are two separate sources of information, and readers should weigh each on its own evidence. Checking primary government files alongside first-hand accounts helps clarify what has been documented.
